Q: The column includes other values ​from the same column A:

First, let's see how a constant word can be searched for:

SELECT ID
FROM T
WHERE WORD LIKE '%infringe%'

Explanation

  • We select from T (you did not provide the name of your table)
  • Where infringe is part of the WORD, as % means "anything" and prepending and appending it to the value you search for you get exactly what you wanted, i.e., the records from T whose WORD contains infringe
  • We select only the ID as specified in the question

Now, if you want to find which records has a WORD that contains other words, you need to get the value dynamically:

SELECT DISTINCT t1.ID
FROM T t1
JOIN T t2
ON t1.ID <> t2.ID AND t1.WORD LIKE '%' || t2.WORD || '%'

Explanation:

  • we select T as t1
  • joined by T as t2
  • on their ID being different and t1.WORD containing t2.WORD
  • and we select t1.ID
  • in a distinct manner to avoid duplicates

Note that in this case 19432 will not be among the results, even though you expected it. The reason is that any WORD contains itself and presumably you don't want to get every record. So if you want to get infringe specifically, then you need to be more lenient with the ON condition, like

SELECT DISTINCT t1.ID
FROM T t1
JOIN T t2
ON (t1.ID <> t2.ID OR t1.WORD = 'infringe') AND t1.WORD LIKE '%' || t2.WORD || '%'

where we only expect the ID to be different for the pairs if the first record's WORD is not an exact match. Here's a screenshot of the test:

EDIT

As Tim Biegeleisen pointed out, we could use EXISTS to for this purpose. I preferred a JOIN in this case with DISTINCT for better readability, but EXISTS is certainly a good option.

Q: Is my recursive CTE failing because of formatting, text encoding or not defined table? A:

Check out MatBailie's answer that fixed the issues that prevented the recursion from happening at all. In addition the source code below is what I ended up on to give my intended actual final result for this recursive query as stated in my question: the sum of the first recurse_number numbers.

with recursive_sum(recurse_number, the_sum) as
(
  select
    1 as recurse_number,
    0 as the_sum
  from dual
  union all
  select
    recurse_number + 1,
    the_sum + recurse_number
  from recursive_sum
  where recurse_number <= 3
)
select max(the_sum) as the_sum from recursive_sum;
